pt.title: Museu da Terra de Miranda reabriu após quatro anos encerrado ao público
pt.description: Museu da Terra de Miranda reabriu após quatro anos encerrado ao público Miranda do Douro mdb Qui, 10/15/2026 - 10:48 O Museu da Terra de Miranda (MTM), em Miranda do Douro, reabriu ao público no sábado em ambiente de festa após quatro encerrado para obras de ampliação requalificação que custaram no seu global 2,4 milhões de euros, que foram repartidos por obras de construção civil e arranjo do espaço expositivo e financiados pelo PRR. Por seu lado, o secretário de Estado da Cultura da Cultura, Alberto Santos, que presidiu à sessão oficial da reabertura do MTM disse durante a cerimónia, que a reabertura do museu é muito representativa porque neste espaço se encontra algo de muito importante que são as suas tradições, os seus ofícios e a língua mirandesa que foram preservadas na imensidão das Arribas do Douro. “É uma satisfação muito grande para a Terra de Miranda, para Trás-os-Montes e sobretudo para Portugal podermos contar com mais este museu, agora renovado, ao serviço da nossa cultura. Este museu vai ajudar a contar a idiossincrasia que esta terra tem, através dos seus elementos culturais, como é sua língua, que foi e é cultivada por muita gente e não desapareceu e que aqui também ganha um novo folgo”, destacou o governante. Alberto Santos destacou ainda, que a leitura do tempo passa pelos ofícios e tradições e que os museus ajudam a contar toda essa história. Já Alexandre Pais, presidente do Conselho de Administração da empresa pública Museus e Monumentos de Portugal destacou a importância a intervenção feita no MTM e demonstrando gratidão ao município de Miranda do Douro e ao Património Cultural I.P. pelo trabalho desenvolvido em colaboração com equipa deste museu para a concretização desta obra. “O MTM é para nós estratégico, porque pensamos nela como um museu do território que está confinado a um espaço geográfico, mas este museu é muito mais do que isso. Ao ser um museu que trabalha o mirandês e os seus testemunhos e por isso um museu de todo o espaço portugueses”, vincou. Para este responsável, o MTM assinala, o novo percurso valoriza o património material e imaterial e coloca no centro não apenas os objetos, mas também as pessoas, as vozes, os saberes e as práticas que lhes dão significado. “A língua e o território, a história, as artes e os ofícios, o espaço doméstico, os trajes, a dança e a música são alguns dos temas que integram esta nova experiência”, acrescentou. Já a presidente da Câmara de Miranda do Douro, Helena Barril, explicou que valeu a pena esperar estes quatro anos, porque há um espaço totalmente renovado, que vai ser devolvido aos mirandeses e ao público em geral. “Este remodelado equipamento será um potenciador da cultura e do turismo em Miranda do Douro e do território. Através deste museu podemos mostrar Miranda ao resto do mundo”, frisou a autarca. A diretora do MTM, Celina Pinto, explicou que a gastronomia, a cutelaria, a tanoaria, as tradições religiosas e populares e o próprio território são alguns dos temas que integram o novo percurso museológico. “A estes junta-se uma dimensão fundamental da identidade local: a língua mirandesa, que surge como língua principal da nova experiência do Museu, que se torna assim no primeiro espaço museológico de Portugal onde convivem o português e o mirandês”, sublinhou. A nova abordagem museológica inclui experiências que convidam a ouvir, tocar e experimentar, reforçando a ligação entre o museu, o território e as suas comunidades através das novas tecnologias de comunicação e interação. As obras de ampliação e beneficiação do MTM, que eram uma ambição bem antiga dos mirandeses, foram iniciadas em 17 de dezembro de 2022. Francisco Pinto Edição 4110

in.title: Impact of El Nino very severe, to reach peak by February: Telangana Chief Secretary
in.description: Telangana Chief Secretary Sanjay Jaju said on Thursday the impact of El Nino is currently 'very severe' and is expected to reach its peak by February 2027. Hyderabad, Oct 15 (IANS) Telangana Chief Secretary Sanjay Jaju said on Thursday the impact of El Nino is currently â€˜very severeâ€™ and is expected to reach its peak by February 2027. He noted that the monsoon has been significantly affected due to El Nino, and temperatures have risen by 2 to 3 degrees Celsius. Talking to media persons after a visit to the Singur Dam, he stated that the government is taking measures to address the current situation. He revealed that the issue will be discussed extensively during the cabinet meeting scheduled for Thursday evening. The Chief Secretary explained that this visit was conducted to assess the outlook for drinking water availability and the status of standing crops. He urged all departments to work in coordination to protect the standing crops over the next 15-20 days. Jaju noted that due to a significant decline in groundwater levels, water may not be available even when electricity is supplied; therefore, he has issued directives to prioritise drinking water needs. He added that nodal officers are being deployed to every district. Under the supervision of the District Collector, officials from the electricity and agriculture departments will remain accessible to farmers on the ground to prepare appropriate plans for the challenges ahead. The Chief Secretary began a field visit in Sangareddy district to assess changes in weather patterns caused by the El Nino, and their impact on water availability in the state. As part of this visit, he inspected water levels at the Singur and Manjira reservoirs. He also held a review meeting with senior officials regarding the implementation of the governmentâ€™s contingency plans, designed to ensure an uninterrupted supply of drinking water to Hyderabad, as well as the districts of Sangareddy, Kamareddy, Nizamabad, and Medak. Given the declining water storage in the Singur and Manjira reservoirs, the Chief Secretary directed officials to ensure the efficient use of available water resources and strictly implement proactive measures to meet future drinking water requirements. He emphasised the need for careful water management -- especially as groundwater levels are falling -- and instructed officials to assess water availability for the next 15 days and take appropriate operational steps accordingly. He directed the relevant departments to closely monitor the impact of these climatic changes on crops. Emphasising that the next 15-20 days are a highly critical period for standing crops, he urged farmers to remain vigilant, and also instructed the Agriculture Department officials to provide necessary guidance to farmers on the ground. The Chief Secretary stated that instructions have been issued to the Electricity Department to ensure an uninterrupted power supply for agricultural needs. He advised the Agriculture, Electricity, and Irrigation Departments to work in coordination, taking into account the current weather conditions and water availability. He further directed officials to personally assess the ground-level situation, engage with farmers and local residents to understand their needs, and raise awareness among the public regarding the proactive measures being taken by the government.

in.title: Shnaider beats Muchova to sail into Wuhan QFs
in.description: Diana Shnaider booked her place in the Wuhan Open quarter-finals on Thursday, defeating Karolina Muchova 7-5, 6-3 to register her fourth career victory against a top-10 opponent and strengthen her campaign at the WTA 1000 event in China. The Russian, who had failed to win a singles or doubles match in her previous two appearances in Wuhan, delivered a composed performance to reach the last eight for the first time, while simultaneously complicating Muchovaâ€™s bid to qualify for the season-ending WTA Finals. The 11th seedâ€™s victory was built on her ability to capitalise when the opening set reached its decisive phase. With Muchova attempting to force another tie-break after surviving two tie-breaks in her previous match against Caty McNally, Shnaider found her opportunity in the 11th game, breaking the Czech after she squandered two consecutive game points. Shnaider then held her nerve to close out the first set 7-5, gaining the advantage in a contest that had remained closely fought until that stage. The breakthrough proved significant as the Russian carried her momentum into the second set. She secured two further breaks of serve while keeping Muchova from mounting a sustained comeback to seal the match in straight sets and advance to her fourth career WTA 1000 quarter-final. The result also extended an impressive run of form for the World No. 13, who has now claimed three of her four career top-10 victories during the 2026 season. Her ability to maintain control throughout the Wuhan campaign has been particularly noteworthy, with all her wins at the tournament coming in straight sets. Shnaiderâ€™s progress adds another strong result to a season in which she has established herself as a consistent contender on the WTA Tour. She entered the Wuhan contest with a 32-20 win-loss record in 2026, having reached the semi-finals at Roland Garros, Adelaide and Washington, alongside quarter-final appearances in Toronto and Charleston. Her performance in Wuhan suggests that the Russian is carrying that consistency into the Asian swing, where another deep run would further strengthen an already productive year. For Muchova, meanwhile, the defeat carries implications beyond her exit from the tournament. The Czech currently has 4,735 points in the live Race to the WTA Finals, ahead of Iga Swiatekâ€™s 3,919. However, Swiatek remains in contention in Wuhan, and winning the title would lift the Polish star to 4,799 points, allowing her to overtake Muchova in the race for the final qualification position. Muchova had entered the match on the back of a demanding three-set victory over McNally, recovering from a set down to win 3-6, 7-6 (1), 7-6 (4). That performance saw her become the first player in the 21st century to win her first 10 tie-breaks of a calendar year. Against Shnaider, however, she could not force another tie-break or reproduce the resilience that had carried her through the previous round. Shnaider will now turn her attention to the quarter-finals, where she is set to face the winner of the encounter between Leylah Fernandez and Jelena Ostapenko. Having arrived in Wuhan without a match victory from her previous two appearances, the Russian has already produced her strongest campaign at the tournament. With a place in the semi-finals now within reach, she will look to build on a performance that combined timely aggression with composure at the crucial moments.

sg.title: ModelBest and OpenBMB Launch MiniCPM-V 4.7, Bringing a 35B Multimodal MoE Model to Phones and Tablets With About 3 GB of Memory
sg.description: BEIJING, Oct. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ModelBest and the OpenBMB community announced the release of MiniCPM-V 4.7, the latest addition to their open-source on-device multimodal model series. Available in 35B-A3B and 1B versions, the release brings advanced image, document and video understanding to edge devices with about 3GB of memory. ModelBest describes MiniCPM-V 4.7 35B-A3B as the first open-source MoE multimodal model built to run smoothly on-device without compromising model quality. The model activates about 3 billion parameters per token and the most experts stay on SSD storage and load as needed, bringing large-model multimodal capability to IOS and Android. It handles general visual understanding, STEM problem solving, OCR, document and chart interpretation, and long-video understanding. According to ModelBest, the model pushes forward the intelligence-cost Pareto frontier for on-device multimodal AI by delivering strong overall performance with short inference time. The 1B version builds on MiniCPM-V 4.6. Designed for lightweight edge devices, it supports general vision, OCR, chart reasoning and multi-image understanding. It can run smoothly on entry-level devices, bringing multimodal AI to more everyday hardware. ModelBest's Lookahead Expert Scheduling (LES) predicts which experts the next layer will need and loads them while the current layer computes. In most scenarios, it prepares more than 80% of required experts in advance without additional training. The model's original router still makes the final expert selection, so outputs are identical with LES enabled or disabled. LES works together with layer-wise quantization and contiguous expert storage. Combined, these optimizations increased average generation speed approximately 5x on an iPad Pro M4 with 16 GB of memory. The model reaches more than 17 tokens per second on that device and more than 13 tokens per second on the iPhone 17 Pro Max. The model also supports both 4× and 16× visual token compression, allowing developers to prioritize detail or speed. At 16× compression, it retains strong performance, scoring 90.9 on MMBench and 90.4 on OCRBench. A new Self-Replay Fine-Tuning method mixes the model's own high-quality responses into training data. This helps the model learn new tasks while retaining its general abilities, at a cost close to standard supervised fine-tuning. MiniCPM-V 4.7 has Day-0 support from AMD, Apple, Arm, Houmo AI, Intel, Rockchip and NVIDIA. Through the FlagOS software stack, it also has Day-0 support for AI and edge chips from CIX Technology, Huawei, Hygon, Iluvatar CoreX, Kunlunxin, MetaX, Moore Threads, Sunrise, T-Head and TsingMicro. Model weights, inference code and fine-tuning code are publicly available for developers to download, evaluate and deploy.

Summary On Thursday, 24 September 2026, Iraq's parliament voted to approve the recommendations of a special committee (Parliamentary Order No. 63) that investigated pollution in the Tigris and Euphrates rivers. Environment Minister Sarwa Abdulwahid declared a state of environmental emergency and announced a platform for reporting and tracking pollution violations, new water-quality monitoring stations, and a one-year government action plan. This is not Iraq's first response to the same rivers this year — it may be at least the fourth. Maysan governorate, one of the three areas behind this month's worst test results, had already declared and then lifted its own local state of emergency over Tigris pollution, ending it around 27 April 2026. Days before that, a different environment minister told the public the wider Tigris-Diyala pollution episode had been "contained." In May, parliament formed a separate special committee, told affected governorates they could sue polluters, and set a six-month deadline for "urgent solutions" to the pollution file — a deadline that does not expire until November, meaning Thursday's vote arrived before its own predecessor's deadline had even run out. In between, a civil-society watchdog publicly asked parliament to convene an urgent session on the crisis in mid-June — three months before it did. The numbers behind these declarations are large by any measure. Government testing reviewed by parliament this month found water failed safety standards in 100 percent of samples in Maysan, 99 percent in Muthanna, and 97 percent in Basra. Roughly six million cubic meters of untreated sewage, medical and industrial waste enter the rivers every day, from more than 500 identifiable sources — many of them state institutions, including hospitals, refineries, and Baghdad's own municipal sewage network. Treatment capacity has not kept pace with any of this. Most of Iraq's water-purification plants have already outlived their 25-year design life. Of 17 small wastewater-treatment units built nationwide, only five are running, and a newly funded Baghdad treatment plant backed by Japanese and World Bank financing has no public construction timeline. The ministry's June reassurance sat alongside its own admission that most sewage goes untreated. In June, it told Iraqis that treated household water was safe — while conceding, in the same statement, that up to 70 percent of sewage in some provinces receives incomplete or no treatment before reaching the rivers. Whether Thursday's declaration breaks the pattern depends on one thing none of the earlier responses delivered: enforcement that reaches inside the state's own institutions, not just a new announcement layered on top of the last one. An emergency declared on a Thursday Iraq's parliament received the report of the Order 63 committee on Wednesday, 23 September, one of four items on that day's agenda alongside a laboratory technicians' bill and an employee-leave law. The committee had been tasked with identifying the causes of pollution in the Tigris and Euphrates, naming the parties responsible, and reviewing what had already been done to limit the damage. A day later, on Thursday, parliament voted to approve its recommendations, and Environment Minister Sarwa Abdulwahid — in the post since mid-May — declared a state of environmental emergency. “Environmental conditions have reached a stage that requires exceptional measures,” she said. The government's response includes a platform for documenting pollution violations and identifying their sources, new water-quality monitoring stations modeled on Iraq's existing air-quality network, and what officials describe as a one-year government action plan. That declaration is a real step: a named minister, a dated vote, and at least two concrete deliverables — a public violations platform and physical monitoring stations — that can be checked later against whether they actually exist. But the emergency itself is not a new discovery, and it is not even the first time this year that the word “emergency” has been formally applied to this same pollution. At some point before mid-April, Maysan governorate — one of the three governorates behind this month's 100/99/97 percent test-failure results — declared its own local state of emergency over Tigris pollution and shut down its water projects as a precaution. On 14 April, national officials said the wider episode had been contained: a sewage leak from the Rustumiya drainage system into the Diyala River, combined with heavy sediment carried by floodwater into the Tigris, had produced a visible crisis around Baghdad — fish die-offs on floating farms, and water tankers dispatched to supply residents in al-Mada'in and Basmaya after local supplies were fouled. The environment minister at the time, Halo al-Askari, announced that ministries and municipalities “were able to contain the phenomenon.” The water resources minister at the same briefing, Aoun Diab, added a warning that proved prescient: “dredging does not fundamentally solve the problem if the sources of pollution are not stopped.” Around two weeks later, on 27 April, Maysan lifted its own emergency, saying laboratory tests had confirmed the water was clean enough to resume normal supply. Three weeks after that, in May, parliament acted again — forming a separate special committee to track pollution in the Diyala and Tigris rivers, directing the governorates affected to pursue lawsuits against polluters, and opening coordination with the United Nations on the environmental damage. One deputy on the committee demanded “urgent solutions” to the pollution file within six months, a deadline that runs to November 2026 and has not yet lapsed — meaning Thursday's vote, and the emergency it declared, landed on top of a still-open commitment from the government's previous attempt at the same problem, not after it. In between, on 14 June, the environmental watchdog Green Iraq Observatory publicly called on parliament to convene an urgent session on the crisis — three months before Order 63's report was actually read into the record. None of this means Thursday's declaration is empty. Governments across the world routinely need more than one attempt to act on slow-moving environmental damage, and a monitoring platform and physical testing stations are a more concrete, checkable commitment than a governorate's decision to reopen its water projects once lab results looked acceptable. But a pattern of a local emergency being declared and lifted, a national “contained” claim, a committee with a deadline still running, and a civil-society call for urgency that took three months to reach the parliamentary floor — all before this week's national emergency — is itself information about how much capacity moved between each of those moments, and how much still has to. The most direct evidence for that is Maysan itself: the same governorate that lifted its own emergency in April on the strength of clean lab results is, five months later, the governorate whose water failed 100 percent of this month's tests. What the rivers actually carry The scale behind this year's run of local, national, and parliamentary responses is not something officials are inventing. Government testing reviewed by a parliamentary health committee this month found that treated water failed safety standards in 100 percent of samples taken in Maysan province, 99 percent in Muthanna, and 97 percent in Basra — the three governorates furthest downstream on the Tigris-Euphrates system, where whatever enters the rivers upstream ends up concentrated. Enlil treats a 100 percent failure rate with some caution, since it likely reflects a specific set of official testing parameters rather than a literal claim that no household tap in Maysan produces potable water. But even a more conservative reading is consistent with Iraq's own longer-run data: World Bank figures put 98 percent of Iraqis as having at least “basic” drinking water and sanitation access, but only about 60 percent have water and about 51 percent have sanitation that meets the stricter WHO/UNICEF standard of being safely managed — free of contamination and reliably available. Iraq built the pipes and the toilets. It did not build the treatment behind them, at the end of a system now receiving an estimated six million cubic meters of untreated sewage, medical waste, and industrial wastewater every day. That volume comes from a source problem too distributed for any single fix. An Al Jazeera investigation in June counted more than 500 identifiable pollution sources discharging into the Tigris and Euphrates between Iraq's northern border and Basra: raw sewage, tannery and industrial effluent, petroleum derivatives, and untreated medical waste. A large share of the named sources are not rogue private actors but the state's own institutions — Baghdad's municipal sewage network, hospitals, and the oil and industrial ministries all appear on the list. A separate parliamentary review this year documented 24 polluted discharge points inside Baghdad alone, including hospital, refinery, and power-station waste, and flagged the Diyala River — already contaminated further upstream — as a concentrator that periodically flushes accumulated sewage and industrial waste toward the Tigris. Iraqi reporting has linked that mechanism to the crisis's most visible symptom: in April, roughly 300 tons of fish died within about two hours in Wasit, and a separate, later incident killed more than 1,000 tons, shutting down downstream water-treatment intakes entirely. Capacity that has not kept pace The infrastructure meant to intercept this volume has aged faster than it has been replaced. Iraq's Green Observatory has found that most water-purification plants nationwide have already exceeded their 25-year design life, a problem most acute in Babylon, Wasit, Anbar, and Salah al-Din. A separate audit of Basra's own treatment plants found that most lack the integrated laboratories needed to test their own output. Where newer capacity exists, it runs far behind demand: Al Jazeera's investigation found 17 small-capacity wastewater-treatment units installed nationally, of which only five are operational — against the 500-plus discharge points documented in the same reporting. A newly funded 300-billion-dinar (roughly $230 million) treatment plant for Baghdad, backed by Japanese and World Bank financing, has no publicly disclosed construction timeline. Five working units against 500 active sources, feeding a system whose existing plants are already past their engineered lifespan, describes a capital-construction gap measured in years — not a shortfall that a one-year action plan, on its own, is built to close. What the ministry's own numbers concede The public argument over how bad the underlying picture is has itself become a recurring feature of this crisis. When similar unfit-water findings circulated in June, the Ministry of Environment publicly maintained that treated household water was safe, citing daily testing across 73 monitoring stations nationwide — while conceding, in the same statement, that roughly 45 percent of Baghdad's sewage and up to 70 percent in other provinces receives incomplete or no treatment before reaching the rivers, which the ministry itself called the biggest challenge to water quality. That concession sits closer to this month's testing data than the reassurance delivered alongside it. Separately, political rhetoric around the crisis has reached for comparisons the evidence does not support: statements this month asserted that water pollution kills or sickens Iraqis at a rate comparable to the country's cumulative terrorism toll, citing rising cancer and kidney-failure cases without an underlying epidemiological study to support the comparison. Enlil treats that comparison as political rhetoric rather than a verified statistic — but notes that no ministry has published the systematic health-outcomes study that would settle the question either way, a gap that leaves the state managing a disputed public-health hazard it has not actually measured. What would make this one different Thursday's declaration is more specific than April's “contained” or May's committee: a named platform for tracking violations, physical water-quality stations, and a one-year plan with a minister's name attached to it. Each of those is a claim that can be checked later, which is itself progress over an assurance that a problem has already been handled. What is not yet confirmed is whether the two other measures reportedly on the table before Thursday's vote — a campaign led by the prime minister's office and amendments to the environmental protection law imposing harsher penalties — were formally adopted alongside the emergency declaration, or remain, like May's lawsuits directive, an instruction that governorates and ministries are free to not fully act on. The test this time is narrower than the declaration itself invites: whether the coming year compels Iraq's own ministries, hospitals, and municipal utilities — named in the government's own data as major sources of the discharge — to fund treatment capacity on a timeline that matches 500 active outlets, succeeding where a governorate's emergency, a national containment claim, and a committee with a still-running deadline have not. A platform that documents violations only has force if violations documented against a state hospital or a state refinery are followed up the same way a violation against a private tannery would be. In Enlil's assessment, that is the ministry's structural position rather than a failing of will: the Ministry of Environment is the regulator, but the largest dischargers in the government's own data are sibling ministries and municipal utilities, over which it has in practice held far less enforcement leverage than over a private firm. Read that way, Thursday's declaration is less a promise by the ministry than a request for authority it has not previously had, and the harsher-penalty amendments still awaiting confirmation are the part that would actually answer it. Iraq will know by November, when the May committee's own deadline runs out, whether Thursday's emergency was the moment Maysan's water stopped failing its tests, or simply the next name given to the same unresolved file.

pk.title: ModelBest and OpenBMB Launch MiniCPM-V 4.7, Bringing a 35B Multimodal MoE Model to Phones and Tablets With About 3 GB of Memory
pk.description: BEIJING, Oct. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ModelBest and the OpenBMB community announced the release of MiniCPM-V 4.7, the latest addition to their open-source on-device multimodal model series. Available in 35B-A3B and 1B versions, the release brings advanced image, document and video understanding to edge devices with about 3GB of memory. ModelBest describes MiniCPM-V 4.7 35B-A3B as the first open-source MoE multimodal model built to run smoothly on-device without compromising model quality. The model activates about 3 billion parameters per token and the most experts stay on SSD storage and load as needed, bringing large-model multimodal capability to IOS and Android. It handles general visual understanding, STEM problem solving, OCR, document and chart interpretation, and long-video understanding. According to ModelBest, the model pushes forward the intelligence-cost Pareto frontier for on-device multimodal AI by delivering strong overall performance with short inference time. The 1B version builds on MiniCPM-V 4.6. Designed for lightweight edge devices, it supports general vision, OCR, chart reasoning and multi-image understanding. It can run smoothly on entry-level devices, bringing multimodal AI to more everyday hardware. ModelBest's Lookahead Expert Scheduling (LES) predicts which experts the next layer will need and loads them while the current layer computes. In most scenarios, it prepares more than 80% of required experts in advance without additional training. The model's original router still makes the final expert selection, so outputs are identical with LES enabled or disabled. LES works together with layer-wise quantization and contiguous expert storage. Combined, these optimizations increased average generation speed approximately 5x on an iPad Pro M4 with 16 GB of memory. The model reaches more than 17 tokens per second on that device and more than 13 tokens per second on the iPhone 17 Pro Max. The model also supports both 4× and 16× visual token compression, allowing developers to prioritize detail or speed. At 16× compression, it retains strong performance, scoring 90.9 on MMBench and 90.4 on OCRBench. A new Self-Replay Fine-Tuning method mixes the model's own high-quality responses into training data. This helps the model learn new tasks while retaining its general abilities, at a cost close to standard supervised fine-tuning. MiniCPM-V 4.7 has Day-0 support from AMD, Apple, Arm, Houmo AI, Intel, Rockchip and NVIDIA. Through the FlagOS software stack, it also has Day-0 support for AI and edge chips from CIX Technology, Huawei, Hygon, Iluvatar CoreX, Kunlunxin, MetaX, Moore Threads, Sunrise, T-Head and TsingMicro. Model weights, inference code and fine-tuning code are publicly available for developers to download, evaluate and deploy.

iq.description: شفق نيوز- أربيل أعلنت مديرية الأنواء الجوية والرصد الزلزالي في إقليم كوردستان، يوم الخميس، عن توقعات الحالة الجوية لليوم وغد الجمعة، مشيرة إلى هطول أمطار متفرقة وزخات رعدية في مناطق متفرقة مع انخفاض طفيف في درجات الحرارة. وقالت المديرية في بيان ورد لوكالة شفق نيوز، إن سماء اليوم الخميس ستكون بين غائمة جزئياً إلى غائمة كلياً، لتبدأ الأمطار بعد ظهر اليوم في الأجزاء الغربية وحدود محافظة دهوك على شكل زخات خفيفة إلى متوسطة، ثم تمتد بشكل متقطع إلى بقية المناطق في أوقات متفرقة، مضيفة أن تأثير الأمطار سيزداد ليلاً في المناطق الشمالية والشمالية الشرقية مع احتمال حدوث بروق ورعد. وأضافت أن الرياح ستكون خفيفة إلى معتدلة السرعة 10-20 كم واتجاهها جنوبي شرقي، بينما يتراوح مدى الرؤية بين 7-9 كم، مع تسجيل ارتفاع طفيف في درجات الحرارة مقارنة بالأمس. وعن طقس يوم غد الجمعة، توقعت الأنواء الجوية أن تكون السماء غائمة كلياً مع استمرار هطول أمطار متقطعة في أغلب المناطق، تتحول أحياناً إلى زخات مطرية مصحوبة برعد، على أن يتراجع تأثير الحالة الجوية خلال ساعات الليل. وأشارت إلى أن درجات الحرارة ستنخفض يوم الجمعة بمعدل 1-2 درجة مئوية مقارنة باليوم، مع رياح شمالية شرقية خفيفة إلى معتدلة ومدى رؤية يتراوح بين (6 - 8 كم). درجات الحرارة العظمى المتوقعة مئوية: أربيل: اليوم 34 - غداً 32 السليمانية: اليوم 32 - غداً 30 دهوك: اليوم 32 - غداً 29 حلبجة: اليوم 32 - غداً 31 بيرمام: اليوم 30 - غداً 28 جمجمال: اليوم 36 - غداً 33 زاخو: اليوم 33 - غداً 31 كرميان: اليوم 36 - غداً 35 حاج عمران: اليوم 22 - غداً 20

إن الجائزة انطلقت عام 2024 بمبادرة من المؤسسة، لتكون منبراً سنوياً للاحتفاء بالإبداع الروائي العربي، وتكريم الأقلام المتميزة، وتشجيع الكتاب على تقديم أعمال تجمع بين القيمة الفنية والرسالة الإنسانية والأخلاقية. وأوضح أن الدورة الثالثة شهدت مشاركة أكثر من 600 رواية، خضعت لمراحل متعددة من الفرز والتقييم عبر اللجان الأولية والرئيسية والعليا، وفق معايير تراعي سلامة اللغة العربية، وجودة السرد والبناء الروائي، ومدى التزام الأعمال بالقيم الأخلاقية والإنسانية. وأضاف الساعدي أن الفائزين ينتمون إلى بلدان عدة، من بينها العراق وتونس والبحرين وفلسطين ومصر ولبنان وفنلندا والأردن والسودان واليمن، بما يعكس التنوع الجغرافي للمشاركات واتساع دائرة التنافس في هذه الدورة. وبيّن أن الجائزة تتوزع على فئتين؛ الأولى لكبار الكتّاب ممن تجاوزوا سن الأربعين، والثانية للشباب دون الأربعين، في مسعى إلى الجمع بين خبرات الأجيال الأدبية الراسخة وطاقات الروائيين الشباب، وإتاحة مساحة أوسع أمام المواهب الجديدة لإثبات حضورها في المشهد الثقافي العربي. وأشار الساعدي إلى أن المؤسسة تتولى الإشراف على الجائزة من النواحي الإدارية والتنظيمية والفنية والأدبية، من خلال لجان متخصصة تعمل على ضمان نزاهة التقييم وشفافيته، بدءاً من استقبال المشاركات وفرزها، وصولاً إلى اعتماد النتائج النهائية. من جانبه، قال مدير جائزة الرواية العربية، نعيم آل مسافر، لوكالة شفق نيوز، إن إعلان النتائج جاء بعد استكمال مراحل تقييم الروايات المشاركة من قبل اللجان المختصة، مؤكداً أن الأعمال الفائزة عكست تجارب روائية من داخل العراق وخارجه. وأضاف آل مسافر أن الجائزة لا تقتصر على تكريم أصحاب الأعمال الفائزة، بل تسعى إلى تشجيع التنافس الأدبي على أساس جودة النص وقيمته الفنية، مع مراعاة المعايير اللغوية والسردية والأخلاقية التي اعتمدتها المؤسسة. جوائز مالية وفرص للوصول إلى القراء وتمنح الجائزة الفائز الأول في كل فئة 15 مليون دينار عراقي، والثاني 10 ملايين دينار، والثالث 7 ملايين و500 ألف دينار، فيما يحصل الفائزون من المركز الرابع إلى العاشر على مليونين و500 ألف دينار لكل فائز. كما تتكفل المؤسسة بطباعة الروايات الفائزة من المراكز العشرة الأولى ونشرها وتسويقها، والمشاركة بها في المعارض الثقافية داخل العراق وخارجه، فضلاً عن تحمل أجور النقل والضيافة للفائزين والضيوف المدعوين من العراق والدول العربية. ومن المقرر أن يتضمن مهرجان الجائزة فعاليات ثقافية وجلسات نقدية إلى جانب توزيع الجوائز، بما يتيح الاحتفاء بالفائزين ومناقشة تجاربهم الروائية، ويفتح نافذة جديدة للتواصل بين الكتّاب والنقاد والمهتمين بالأدب. وتسعى جائزة الرواية العربية، وفق القائمين عليها، إلى جعل الرواية مساحة للإبداع والتجديد، ووسيلة لاستكشاف التجارب الإنسانية، وتعزيز حضور الأدب الذي يلتقي فيه جمال الكلمة مع القيم الأخلاقية، انطلاقاً من شعارها "وإنما تحيا الأمم بأخلاقها"

tn.description: أكد المجلس الوطني للجهات والأقاليم، في بيان أصدره اليوم الخميس 15 أكتوبر، بمناسبة ذكرى الجلاء أن حماية الدّولة ومؤسساتها وصون أمنها واستقرارها مسؤولية وطنية جامعة، تستوجب اليقظة في مواجهة كل ما من شأنه المساس بمصالح الوطن العليا أو النيل من تماسكه. وجدد المجلس في ذات البيان، رفضه القاطع كُلّ أشكال العمالة والارتهان والتبعيّة، وكلّ محاولة تستهدف إخضاع الإرادة التونسية أو فرض الوصاية على قرارها الوطني أو إعادة إنتاج النفوذ الاستعماري بأشكال جديدة، وأكد المجلس حق تونس في اختيار مسارها ورسم خياراتها وفق إرادة شعبها ومصالحه العليا، وصون استقلال قرارها من كل إملاء أو تدخّل. وشدد على أن صون مكاسب الاستقلال يقتضي تعزيز مقوّمات القوة الوطنية، من خلال حماية الثروات والمقدّرات، ودعم الإنتاج الوطني، وتثمين الكفاءات والطاقات التونسية، وتطوير قدرة الاقتصاد على الصمود، بما يعزز استقلالية الخيارات الاقتصادية والاجتماعية ويوجّه إمكانات البلاد نحو خدمة الشعب وضمان مستقبل أفضل للأجيال القادمة.
